237	def generate_arc_path(poses: np.ndarray,
238	                      n_frames: int = 120,
239	                      scale_factor: float = 1.0,
240	                      arc_extension: float = -0.1,
241	                      clockwise: bool = True) -> np.ndarray: 
242	    """
243	    Generate an elliptical arc path that covers only the visible portion.
244	    
245	    Args:
246	        poses: Input camera poses
247	        n_frames: Number of frames to generate
248	        scale_factor: Scale factor for the ellipse size
249	        arc_extension: Extra arc length beyond input cameras
250	        clockwise: If True, camera moves clockwise (从上往下看); if False, counter-clockwise
251	    """
252	    print("\n" + "="*70)
253	    print("  Generating Ellipse Arc Camera Path")
254	    print("="*70)
255	    
256	    # Find the focus point
257	    center = focus_point_fn(poses)
258	    print(f"\n[1] Ellipse Center (Focal Point):")
259	    print(f"    Position: [{center[0]:.4f}, {center[1]:.4f}, {center[2]:.4f}]")
260	    
261	    # Get camera positions
262	    positions = poses[:, :3, 3]
263	    
264	    # Fit an ellipse to the camera positions
265	    plane_normal, major_axis, minor_axis, semi_major, semi_minor = fit_ellipse_to_points(positions, center)
266	    
267	    print(f"\n[2] Fitted Ellipse Parameters:")
268	    print(f"    Semi-major axis: {semi_major:.4f}")
269	    print(f"    Semi-minor axis: {semi_minor:.4f}")
270	    print(f"    Plane normal: [{plane_normal[0]:.4f}, {plane_normal[1]:.4f}, {plane_normal[2]:.4f}]")
271	    
272	    
273	    ellipse_normal = np.cross(major_axis, minor_axis)
274	    ellipse_normal = ellipse_normal / np.linalg.norm(ellipse_normal)
275	    
276	    up = estimate_up_vector(poses, center)
277	    reference_up = up / np.linalg.norm(up)
278	    
279	    if np.dot(ellipse_normal, reference_up) < 0:
280	        minor_axis = -minor_axis
281	        ellipse_normal = -ellipse_normal
282	        print(f"\n[*] Flipped minor_axis to align with reference up vector")
283	    
284	    print(f"    Ellipse normal (aligned): [{ellipse_normal[0]:.4f}, {ellipse_normal[1]:.4f}, {ellipse_normal[2]:.4f}]")
285	    
286	    # Scale the ellipse
287	    semi_major *= scale_factor
288	    semi_minor *= scale_factor
289	    
290	    # Calculate angles of input cameras
291	    centered_positions = positions - center
292	    input_angles = []
293	    
294	    for pos in centered_positions:
295	        x = np.dot(pos, major_axis)
296	        y = np.dot(pos, minor_axis)
297	        angle = np.arctan2(y / semi_minor, x / semi_major)
298	        input_angles.append(angle)
299	    
300	    input_angles = np.array(input_angles)
301	    
302	    angles_normalized = np.mod(input_angles, 2 * np.pi)
303	    span_raw = np.max(input_angles) - np.min(input_angles)
304	    span_normalized = np.max(angles_normalized) - np.min(angles_normalized)
305	    wraps_around = span_normalized < span_raw - np.pi
306	    
307	    if wraps_around:
308	        angles_unwrapped = np.where(input_angles < 0, input_angles + 2*np.pi, input_angles)
309	        min_angle = np.min(angles_unwrapped)
310	        max_angle = np.max(angles_unwrapped)
311	        print(f"\n[4] Detected wrap-around at 0°")
312	    else:
313	        min_angle = np.min(input_angles)
314	        max_angle = np.max(input_angles)
315	        print(f"\n[4] No wrap-around detected")
316	    
317	    angle_span = max_angle - min_angle
318	    
319	    print(f"    Min angle: {np.degrees(min_angle):7.2f}°")
320	    print(f"    Max angle: {np.degrees(max_angle):7.2f}°")
321	    print(f"    Span: {np.degrees(angle_span):7.2f}°")
322	    
323	    # Extend the arc
324	    arc_padding = angle_span * abs(arc_extension)
325	    arc_start = min_angle - arc_padding
326	    arc_end = max_angle + arc_padding
327	    
328	    print(f"\n[5] Arc Extension:")
329	    print(f"    Extension: ±{np.degrees(arc_padding):7.2f}°")
330	    print(f"    Arc start: {np.degrees(arc_start):7.2f}°")
331	    print(f"    Arc end: {np.degrees(arc_end):7.2f}°")
332	    print(f"    Total arc: {np.degrees(arc_end - arc_start):7.2f}°")
333	    
334	    
335	    if not clockwise:  
336	        theta = np.linspace(arc_start, arc_end, n_frames, endpoint=True)
337	        print(f"\n[*] Direction: COUNTER-CLOCKWISE (angle increasing)")
338	    else:  
339	        theta = np.linspace(arc_end, arc_start, n_frames, endpoint=True)
340	        print(f"\n[*] Direction: CLOCKWISE (angle decreasing)")
341	    
342	    # Generate points along the arc
343	    ellipse_positions = np.zeros((n_frames, 3))
344	    for i, t in enumerate(theta):
345	        offset = semi_major * np.cos(t) * major_axis + semi_minor * np.sin(t) * minor_axis
346	        ellipse_positions[i] = center + offset
347	    
348	    print(f"\n[6] Up Vector:")
349	    print(f"    Direction: [{up[0]:.4f}, {up[1]:.4f}, {up[2]:.4f}]")
350	    
351	    # Generate camera poses
352	    camera_poses = np.stack([viewmatrix(p - center, up, p) for p in ellipse_positions])
353	    
354	    print(f"\n[7] Path Direction Verification:")
355	    print(f"    First frame angle: {np.degrees(theta[0]):7.2f}°")
356	    print(f"    Last frame angle: {np.degrees(theta[-1]):7.2f}°")
357	    print(f"    Angle change: {np.degrees(theta[-1] - theta[0]):7.2f}°")
358	    
359	    mid_idx = len(theta) // 2
360	    pos_start = ellipse_positions[0] - center
361	    pos_mid = ellipse_positions[mid_idx] - center
362	    pos_end = ellipse_positions[-1] - center
363	    
364	    cross1 = np.cross(pos_start, pos_mid)
365	    cross2 = np.cross(pos_mid, pos_end)
366	    avg_cross = (cross1 + cross2) / 2
367	    
368	    rotation_direction = "COUNTER-CLOCKWISE" if np.dot(avg_cross, ellipse_normal) > 0 else "CLOCKWISE"
369	    print(f"    Physical rotation: {rotation_direction}")
370	    print(f"    Expected rotation: {'CLOCKWISE' if clockwise else 'COUNTER-CLOCKWISE'}")
371	    
372	    if (clockwise and rotation_direction == "CLOCKWISE") or \
373	       (not clockwise and rotation_direction == "COUNTER-CLOCKWISE"):
374	        print(f"    ✓ Direction matches expectation!")
375	    else:
376	        print(f"    ✗ WARNING: Direction mismatch!")
377	    
378	    print(f"\n✓ Successfully generated {n_frames} camera poses")
379	    print("="*70 + "\n")
380	    
381	    return camera_poses

383	def generate_path(viewpoint_cameras, n_frames=480, traj='ellipse', scale_factor=1.0, total_frames=300, fix_time=False, selected_frame=-1):
384	
385	    # Sample cameras
386	    viewpoint_cameras = [viewpoint_cameras[i] for i in range(0, len(viewpoint_cameras), total_frames)]
387	    
388	    c2ws = np.array([np.linalg.inv(np.asarray((cam[1].world_view_transform.T).cpu().numpy())) 
389	                     for cam in viewpoint_cameras])
390	    
391	    poses = c2ws[:, :3, :] @ np.diag([1, -1, -1, 1])
392	    
393	    # Generate new poses based on trajectory type
394	    if traj == 'ellipse':
395	        pose_recenter, colmap_to_world_transform = transform_poses_pca(poses)
396	        new_poses = generate_ellipse_path(poses=pose_recenter, n_frames=n_frames, scale_factor=scale_factor)
397	        new_poses = np.linalg.inv(colmap_to_world_transform) @ pad_poses(new_poses)
398	    elif traj == 'interpolate':
399	        new_poses = generate_smooth_interpolation_path(poses=poses, n_frames=n_frames)
400	    elif traj == 'arc':
401	        new_poses = generate_arc_path(poses=poses, n_frames=n_frames, scale_factor=scale_factor, clockwise=False)
402	    else:
403	        raise ValueError(f'Trajectory type {traj} not supported.')
404	
405	    new_poses = new_poses @ np.diag([1, -1, -1, 1])
406	    
407	    if selected_frame >= 0:
408	        new_poses = [new_poses[selected_frame]] * n_frames
409	        
410	    traj_archived = traj
411	    # Create camera objects
412	    traj = []
413	    for i, pose_3x4 in enumerate(new_poses):
414	        cam = copy.deepcopy(viewpoint_cameras[0][1])
415	        cam.image_height = int(cam.image_height / 2) * 2
416	        cam.image_width = int(cam.image_width / 2) * 2
417	        
418	        if traj_archived != 'ellipse':
419	            c2w_4x4 = np.eye(4)
420	            c2w_4x4[:3, :] = pose_3x4
421	            w2c_4x4 = np.linalg.inv(c2w_4x4)
422	            cam.world_view_transform = torch.from_numpy(w2c_4x4.T).float().cuda()
423	        else:
424	            cam.world_view_transform = torch.from_numpy(np.linalg.inv(pose_3x4).T).float().cuda()
425	            
426	        cam.full_proj_transform = (cam.world_view_transform.unsqueeze(0).bmm(
427	            cam.projection_matrix.cuda().unsqueeze(0))).squeeze(0)
428	        cam.camera_center = cam.world_view_transform.inverse()[3, :3]
429	        if not fix_time:
430	            cam.timestamp = 10.0 / n_frames * i
431	        else:
432	            cam.timestamp = 10.0 / n_frames * i * total_frames / 300.0
433	        traj.append(cam)
434	    
435	    return traj

import numpy as np
import os
import copy
from PIL import Image
import mediapy as media
from matplotlib import cm
from tqdm import tqdm
import torch

from scipy.interpolate import splprep, splev

def normalize(x: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Normalization helper function."""
    return x / (np.linalg.norm(x) + 1e-8)

def pad_poses(p: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Pad [..., 3, 4] pose matrices with a homogeneous bottom row [0,0,0,1]."""
    bottom = np.broadcast_to([0, 0, 0, 1.], p[..., :1, :4].shape)
    return np.concatenate([p[..., :3, :4], bottom], axis=-2)

def unpad_poses(p: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Remove the homogeneous bottom row from [..., 4, 4] pose matrices."""
    return p[..., :3, :4]

def viewmatrix(lookdir: np.ndarray, up: np.ndarray, position: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Construct lookat view matrix."""
    vec2 = normalize(lookdir)
    vec0 = normalize(np.cross(up, vec2))
    vec1 = normalize(np.cross(vec2, vec0))
    m = np.stack([vec0, vec1, vec2, position], axis=1)
    return m

def focus_point_fn(poses: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Calculate nearest point to all focal axes in poses."""
    directions, origins = poses[:, :3, 2:3], poses[:, :3, 3:4]
    m = np.eye(3) - directions * np.transpose(directions, [0, 2, 1])
    mt_m = np.transpose(m, [0, 2, 1]) @ m
    focus_pt = np.linalg.inv(mt_m.mean(0)) @ (mt_m @ origins).mean(0)[:, 0]
    return focus_pt

def estimate_up_vector(poses: np.ndarray, focus_point: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Estimate a consistent up vector from camera poses.
    Uses the average Y-axis (up direction) of all cameras.
    """
    # Method 1: Average of all camera Y-axes
    up_vectors = poses[:, :3, 1]  # Extract Y-axis from all poses
    avg_up = np.mean(up_vectors, axis=0)
    avg_up = normalize(avg_up)
    
    # Method 2: Ensure up vector is perpendicular to average view direction
    positions = poses[:, :3, 3]
    avg_view_dir = normalize(focus_point - np.mean(positions, axis=0))
    
    # Make up perpendicular to view direction
    avg_up = avg_up - np.dot(avg_up, avg_view_dir) * avg_view_dir
    avg_up = normalize(avg_up)
    
    return avg_up

def fit_ellipse_to_points(points: np.ndarray, center: np.ndarray) -> tuple:
    """
    Fit an ellipse to 3D points around a center.
    Returns: (plane_normal, major_axis, minor_axis, semi_major, semi_minor)
    """
    # Center the points
    centered_points = points - center
    
    # Use PCA to find the best-fit plane
    _, _, Vt = np.linalg.svd(centered_points)
    plane_normal = Vt[-1]  # Normal is the smallest singular vector
    
    # Project points onto the plane
    # Create orthonormal basis for the plane
    major_axis = Vt[0]  # Direction of maximum variance
    minor_axis = np.cross(plane_normal, major_axis)
    minor_axis = normalize(minor_axis)
    
    # Project points onto the two plane axes
    x_coords = np.dot(centered_points, major_axis)
    y_coords = np.dot(centered_points, minor_axis)
    
    # Estimate semi-axes lengths
    semi_major = np.max(np.abs(x_coords))
    semi_minor = np.max(np.abs(y_coords))
    
    return plane_normal, major_axis, minor_axis, semi_major, semi_minor

def transform_poses_pca(poses: np.ndarray):
    """Transforms poses so principal components lie on XYZ axes.
    Args:
        poses: a (N, 3, 4) array containing the cameras' camera to world transforms.
    Returns:
        A tuple (poses, transform), with the transformed poses and the applied
        camera_to_world transforms.
    """
    t = poses[:, :3, 3]
    t_mean = t.mean(axis=0)
    t = t - t_mean

    eigval, eigvec = np.linalg.eig(t.T @ t)
    # Sort eigenvectors in order of largest to smallest eigenvalue.
    inds = np.argsort(eigval)[::-1]
    eigvec = eigvec[:, inds]
    rot = eigvec.T
    if np.linalg.det(rot) < 0:
        rot = np.diag(np.array([1, 1, -1])) @ rot

    transform = np.concatenate([rot, rot @ -t_mean[:, None]], -1)
    poses_recentered = unpad_poses(transform @ pad_poses(poses))
    transform = np.concatenate([transform, np.eye(4)[3:]], axis=0)

    # Flip coordinate system if z component of y-axis is negative
    if poses_recentered.mean(axis=0)[2, 1] < 0:
        poses_recentered = np.diag(np.array([1, -1, -1])) @ poses_recentered
        transform = np.diag(np.array([1, -1, -1, 1])) @ transform

    return poses_recentered, transform

def generate_ellipse_path(poses: np.ndarray,
                          n_frames: int = 120,
                          const_speed: bool = True,
                          z_variation: float = 0.,
                          z_phase: float = 0.,
                          scale_factor: float = 1.0) -> np.ndarray:
    """Generate an elliptical render path based on the given poses."""
    # Calculate the focal point for the path (cameras point toward this).
    center = focus_point_fn(poses)
    z_base = np.min(poses[:, :3, 3][:, 2]) # z_median or z_mean = 0, center[2] is not available

    # Path height sits at z=0 (in middle of zero-mean capture pattern).
    offset = np.array([center[0], center[1], z_base])

    # Calculate scaling for ellipse axes based on input camera positions.
    sc = np.percentile(np.abs(poses[:, :3, 3] - offset), 90, axis=0) * scale_factor
    # sc = np.min(np.abs(poses[:, :3, 3] - offset), axis=0) * scale_factor

    # Use ellipse that is symmetric about the focal point in xy.
    low = -sc + offset
    high = sc + offset
    # Optional height variation need not be symmetric
    z_low = np.percentile((poses[:, :3, 3]), 10, axis=0)
    z_high = np.percentile((poses[:, :3, 3]), 90, axis=0)

    def get_positions(theta):
        # Interpolate between bounds with trig functions to get ellipse in x-y.
        # Optionally also interpolate in z to change camera height along path.
        return np.stack([
            low[0] + (high - low)[0] * (np.cos(theta) * .5 + .5),
            low[1] + (high - low)[1] * (np.sin(theta) * .5 + .5),
            z_base + z_variation * (z_low[2] + (z_high - z_low)[2] *
                        (np.cos(theta + 2 * np.pi * z_phase) * .5 + .5)),
        ], -1)

    theta = np.linspace(0, 2. * np.pi, n_frames + 1, endpoint=True)
    positions = get_positions(theta)

    # Throw away duplicated last position.
    positions = positions[:-1]

    # Set path's up vector to axis closest to average of input pose up vectors.
    avg_up = poses[:, :3, 1].mean(0)
    avg_up = avg_up / np.linalg.norm(avg_up)
    ind_up = np.argmax(np.abs(avg_up))
    up = np.eye(3)[ind_up] * np.sign(avg_up[ind_up])

    return np.stack([viewmatrix(p - center, up, p) for p in positions])

def generate_smooth_interpolation_path(poses: np.ndarray,
                                       n_frames: int = 120,
                                       smoothness: float = 0.0) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Generate a smooth interpolation path through all input camera positions using splines.
    
    Args:
        poses: Input camera poses
        n_frames: Number of frames to generate
        smoothness: Smoothing parameter for spline (0 = pass through all points exactly)
    """
    # Find the focus point
    center = focus_point_fn(poses)
    
    # Get camera positions
    positions = poses[:, :3, 3]
    n_input = len(positions)
    
    # Sort positions by angle around the focus point (for closed loop)
    centered = positions - center
    
    # Project onto best-fit plane to get 2D angles
    _, _, Vt = np.linalg.svd(centered)
    basis_x = Vt[0]
    basis_y = Vt[1]
    
    x_coords = np.dot(centered, basis_x)
    y_coords = np.dot(centered, basis_y)
    angles = np.arctan2(y_coords, x_coords)
    
    # Sort by angle
    sort_idx = np.argsort(angles)
    positions_sorted = positions[sort_idx]
    
    # Add first point at end to close the loop
    positions_loop = np.vstack([positions_sorted, positions_sorted[0:1]])
    
    # Fit a smooth spline through the positions
    tck, u = splprep([positions_loop[:, 0], positions_loop[:, 1], positions_loop[:, 2]], 
                     s=smoothness, per=True)
    
    # Evaluate spline at n_frames points
    u_new = np.linspace(0, 1, n_frames, endpoint=False)
    interpolated = splev(u_new, tck)
    interpolated_positions = np.column_stack(interpolated)
    
    # Estimate up vector
    up = estimate_up_vector(poses, center)
    
    # Generate camera poses
    camera_poses = np.stack([viewmatrix(p - center, up, p) for p in interpolated_positions])
    
    return camera_poses

def generate_arc_path(poses: np.ndarray,
                      n_frames: int = 120,
                      scale_factor: float = 1.0,
                      arc_extension: float = -0.1,
                      clockwise: bool = True) -> np.ndarray: 
    """
    Generate an elliptical arc path that covers only the visible portion.
    
    Args:
        poses: Input camera poses
        n_frames: Number of frames to generate
        scale_factor: Scale factor for the ellipse size
        arc_extension: Extra arc length beyond input cameras
        clockwise: If True, camera moves clockwise (从上往下看); if False, counter-clockwise
    """
    print("\n" + "="*70)
    print("  Generating Ellipse Arc Camera Path")
    print("="*70)
    
    # Find the focus point
    center = focus_point_fn(poses)
    print(f"\n[1] Ellipse Center (Focal Point):")
    print(f"    Position: [{center[0]:.4f}, {center[1]:.4f}, {center[2]:.4f}]")
    
    # Get camera positions
    positions = poses[:, :3, 3]
    
    # Fit an ellipse to the camera positions
    plane_normal, major_axis, minor_axis, semi_major, semi_minor = fit_ellipse_to_points(positions, center)
    
    print(f"\n[2] Fitted Ellipse Parameters:")
    print(f"    Semi-major axis: {semi_major:.4f}")
    print(f"    Semi-minor axis: {semi_minor:.4f}")
    print(f"    Plane normal: [{plane_normal[0]:.4f}, {plane_normal[1]:.4f}, {plane_normal[2]:.4f}]")
    
    
    ellipse_normal = np.cross(major_axis, minor_axis)
    ellipse_normal = ellipse_normal / np.linalg.norm(ellipse_normal)
    
    up = estimate_up_vector(poses, center)
    reference_up = up / np.linalg.norm(up)
    
    if np.dot(ellipse_normal, reference_up) < 0:
        minor_axis = -minor_axis
        ellipse_normal = -ellipse_normal
        print(f"\n[*] Flipped minor_axis to align with reference up vector")
    
    print(f"    Ellipse normal (aligned): [{ellipse_normal[0]:.4f}, {ellipse_normal[1]:.4f}, {ellipse_normal[2]:.4f}]")
    
    # Scale the ellipse
    semi_major *= scale_factor
    semi_minor *= scale_factor
    
    # Calculate angles of input cameras
    centered_positions = positions - center
    input_angles = []
    
    for pos in centered_positions:
        x = np.dot(pos, major_axis)
        y = np.dot(pos, minor_axis)
        angle = np.arctan2(y / semi_minor, x / semi_major)
        input_angles.append(angle)
    
    input_angles = np.array(input_angles)
    
    angles_normalized = np.mod(input_angles, 2 * np.pi)
    span_raw = np.max(input_angles) - np.min(input_angles)
    span_normalized = np.max(angles_normalized) - np.min(angles_normalized)
    wraps_around = span_normalized < span_raw - np.pi
    
    if wraps_around:
        angles_unwrapped = np.where(input_angles < 0, input_angles + 2*np.pi, input_angles)
        min_angle = np.min(angles_unwrapped)
        max_angle = np.max(angles_unwrapped)
        print(f"\n[4] Detected wrap-around at 0°")
    else:
        min_angle = np.min(input_angles)
        max_angle = np.max(input_angles)
        print(f"\n[4] No wrap-around detected")
    
    angle_span = max_angle - min_angle
    
    print(f"    Min angle: {np.degrees(min_angle):7.2f}°")
    print(f"    Max angle: {np.degrees(max_angle):7.2f}°")
    print(f"    Span: {np.degrees(angle_span):7.2f}°")
    
    # Extend the arc
    arc_padding = angle_span * abs(arc_extension)
    arc_start = min_angle - arc_padding
    arc_end = max_angle + arc_padding
    
    print(f"\n[5] Arc Extension:")
    print(f"    Extension: ±{np.degrees(arc_padding):7.2f}°")
    print(f"    Arc start: {np.degrees(arc_start):7.2f}°")
    print(f"    Arc end: {np.degrees(arc_end):7.2f}°")
    print(f"    Total arc: {np.degrees(arc_end - arc_start):7.2f}°")
    
    
    if not clockwise:  
        theta = np.linspace(arc_start, arc_end, n_frames, endpoint=True)
        print(f"\n[*] Direction: COUNTER-CLOCKWISE (angle increasing)")
    else:  
        theta = np.linspace(arc_end, arc_start, n_frames, endpoint=True)
        print(f"\n[*] Direction: CLOCKWISE (angle decreasing)")
    
    # Generate points along the arc
    ellipse_positions = np.zeros((n_frames, 3))
    for i, t in enumerate(theta):
        offset = semi_major * np.cos(t) * major_axis + semi_minor * np.sin(t) * minor_axis
        ellipse_positions[i] = center + offset
    
    print(f"\n[6] Up Vector:")
    print(f"    Direction: [{up[0]:.4f}, {up[1]:.4f}, {up[2]:.4f}]")
    
    # Generate camera poses
    camera_poses = np.stack([viewmatrix(p - center, up, p) for p in ellipse_positions])
    
    print(f"\n[7] Path Direction Verification:")
    print(f"    First frame angle: {np.degrees(theta[0]):7.2f}°")
    print(f"    Last frame angle: {np.degrees(theta[-1]):7.2f}°")
    print(f"    Angle change: {np.degrees(theta[-1] - theta[0]):7.2f}°")
    
    mid_idx = len(theta) // 2
    pos_start = ellipse_positions[0] - center
    pos_mid = ellipse_positions[mid_idx] - center
    pos_end = ellipse_positions[-1] - center
    
    cross1 = np.cross(pos_start, pos_mid)
    cross2 = np.cross(pos_mid, pos_end)
    avg_cross = (cross1 + cross2) / 2
    
    rotation_direction = "COUNTER-CLOCKWISE" if np.dot(avg_cross, ellipse_normal) > 0 else "CLOCKWISE"
    print(f"    Physical rotation: {rotation_direction}")
    print(f"    Expected rotation: {'CLOCKWISE' if clockwise else 'COUNTER-CLOCKWISE'}")
    
    if (clockwise and rotation_direction == "CLOCKWISE") or \
       (not clockwise and rotation_direction == "COUNTER-CLOCKWISE"):
        print(f"    ✓ Direction matches expectation!")
    else:
        print(f"    ✗ WARNING: Direction mismatch!")
    
    print(f"\n✓ Successfully generated {n_frames} camera poses")
    print("="*70 + "\n")
    
    return camera_poses

def generate_path(viewpoint_cameras, n_frames=480, traj='ellipse', scale_factor=1.0, total_frames=300, fix_time=False, selected_frame=-1):

    # Sample cameras
    viewpoint_cameras = [viewpoint_cameras[i] for i in range(0, len(viewpoint_cameras), total_frames)]
    
    c2ws = np.array([np.linalg.inv(np.asarray((cam[1].world_view_transform.T).cpu().numpy())) 
                     for cam in viewpoint_cameras])
    
    poses = c2ws[:, :3, :] @ np.diag([1, -1, -1, 1])
    
    # Generate new poses based on trajectory type
    if traj == 'ellipse':
        pose_recenter, colmap_to_world_transform = transform_poses_pca(poses)
        new_poses = generate_ellipse_path(poses=pose_recenter, n_frames=n_frames, scale_factor=scale_factor)
        new_poses = np.linalg.inv(colmap_to_world_transform) @ pad_poses(new_poses)
    elif traj == 'interpolate':
        new_poses = generate_smooth_interpolation_path(poses=poses, n_frames=n_frames)
    elif traj == 'arc':
        new_poses = generate_arc_path(poses=poses, n_frames=n_frames, scale_factor=scale_factor, clockwise=False)
    else:
        raise ValueError(f'Trajectory type {traj} not supported.')

    new_poses = new_poses @ np.diag([1, -1, -1, 1])
    
    if selected_frame >= 0:
        new_poses = [new_poses[selected_frame]] * n_frames
        
    traj_archived = traj
    # Create camera objects
    traj = []
    for i, pose_3x4 in enumerate(new_poses):
        cam = copy.deepcopy(viewpoint_cameras[0][1])
        cam.image_height = int(cam.image_height / 2) * 2
        cam.image_width = int(cam.image_width / 2) * 2
        
        if traj_archived != 'ellipse':
            c2w_4x4 = np.eye(4)
            c2w_4x4[:3, :] = pose_3x4
            w2c_4x4 = np.linalg.inv(c2w_4x4)
            cam.world_view_transform = torch.from_numpy(w2c_4x4.T).float().cuda()
        else:
            cam.world_view_transform = torch.from_numpy(np.linalg.inv(pose_3x4).T).float().cuda()
            
        cam.full_proj_transform = (cam.world_view_transform.unsqueeze(0).bmm(
            cam.projection_matrix.cuda().unsqueeze(0))).squeeze(0)
        cam.camera_center = cam.world_view_transform.inverse()[3, :3]
        if not fix_time:
            cam.timestamp = 10.0 / n_frames * i
        else:
            cam.timestamp = 10.0 / n_frames * i * total_frames / 300.0
        traj.append(cam)
    
    return traj

def load_img(pth: str) -> np.ndarray:
    """Load an image and cast to float32."""
    with open(pth, 'rb') as f:
        image = np.array(Image.open(f), dtype=np.float32)
    return image

def create_videos(base_dir, input_dir, out_name, num_frames=480):
    """Creates videos out of the images saved to disk."""
    # Last two parts of checkpoint path are experiment name and scene name.
    video_prefix = f'{out_name}'
    zpad = max(5, len(str(num_frames - 1)))
    idx_to_str = lambda idx: str(idx).zfill(zpad)

    os.makedirs(base_dir, exist_ok=True)
    render_dist_curve_fn = np.log

    # Load one example frame to get image shape and depth range.
    color_file = os.path.join(input_dir, 'renders', f'{idx_to_str(0)}.png')
    color_frame = load_img(color_file)
    shape = color_frame.shape
    p = 3
    distance_limits = np.percentile(color_frame.flatten(), [p, 100 - p])
    lo, hi = [render_dist_curve_fn(x) for x in distance_limits]
    print(f'Video shape is {shape[:2]}')

    video_kwargs = {
        'shape': shape[:2],
        'codec': 'h264',
        'fps': 48,
        'crf': 18,
    }

    for k in ['depth', 'normal', 'color','flow']:
        video_file = os.path.join(base_dir, f'{video_prefix}_{k}.mp4')
        input_format = 'gray' if k == 'alpha' else 'rgb'

        file_ext = 'png' if k in ['color', 'normal','flow'] else 'tiff'
        idx = 0

        if k == 'color':
            file0 = os.path.join(input_dir, 'renders', f'{idx_to_str(0)}.{file_ext}')
        elif k=='flow':
            file0 = os.path.join(input_dir, 'flow', f'{k}_{idx_to_str(0)}.{file_ext}')
        else:
            file0 = os.path.join(input_dir, 'vis', f'{k}_{idx_to_str(0)}.{file_ext}')

        if not os.path.exists(file0):
            print(f'Images missing for tag {k}')
            continue
        print(f'Making video {video_file}...')
        with media.VideoWriter(video_file, **video_kwargs, input_format=input_format) as writer:
            for idx in tqdm(range(num_frames)):
                # img_file = os.path.join(input_dir, f'{k}_{idx_to_str(idx)}.{file_ext}')
                if k == 'color':
                    img_file = os.path.join(input_dir, 'renders', f'{idx_to_str(idx)}.{file_ext}')
                elif k=='flow':
                    img_file = os.path.join(input_dir, 'flow', f'{idx_to_str(idx)}.{file_ext}')
                else:
                    img_file = os.path.join(input_dir, 'vis', f'{k}_{idx_to_str(idx)}.{file_ext}')

                if not os.path.exists(img_file):
                    ValueError(f'Image file {img_file} does not exist.')
                img = load_img(img_file)

                if k in ['color', 'normal', 'flow']:
                    img = img / 255.
                elif k.startswith('depth'):
                    img = render_dist_curve_fn(img)
                    img = np.clip((img - np.minimum(lo, hi)) / np.abs(hi - lo), 0, 1)
                    img = cm.get_cmap('turbo')(img)[..., :3]

                frame = (np.clip(np.nan_to_num(img), 0., 1.) * 255.).astype(np.uint8)
                writer.add_image(frame)
                idx += 1

def save_img_u8(img, pth):
    """Save an image (probably RGB) in [0, 1] to disk as a uint8 PNG."""
    with open(pth, 'wb') as f:
        Image.fromarray(
            (np.clip(np.nan_to_num(img), 0., 1.) * 255.).astype(np.uint8)).save(
                f, 'PNG')

def save_img_f32(depthmap, pth):
    """Save an image (probably a depthmap) to disk as a float32 TIFF."""
    with open(pth, 'wb') as f:
        Image.fromarray(np.nan_to_num(depthmap).astype(np.float32)).save(f, 'TIFF')

   - `export_image`（L216-225）：renders/*.png + vis/depth_*.tiff
   - `reconstruction_and_export`（L227-426）：渲染与导出同步，省显存
2. **generate_path 的轨迹消费端**（utils/render_utils.py L383-435）——u7-l2 已经详细讲过 generate_path 的数据流，本讲承接它的输出（480 个 Camera 对象列表），不重复。
3. **create_videos**（utils/render_utils.py L443-510）：mediapy VideoWriter，h264、fps=48、crf=18，四类视频 depth/normal/color/flow，颜色视频从 renders/ 读 png，depth 从 vis/ 读 tiff 并 log+turbo colormap。
4. **save_img_u8 / save_img_f32**（L512-521）
5. **render.py 中 traj 分支**（L63-75）：n_frames=480，generate_path → reconstruction(stage="trajectory") → export_image → create_videos

## 输出结构
```
<model_path>/traj/ours_<first_iter>/
├── renders/
│   ├── 00000.png
│   ├── 00001.png
│   └── ... (480 帧)
├── vis/
│   ├── depth_00000.tiff
│   └── ...
└── <name>_<traj>_scale<scale_factor>_<MMDDHHMM>_color.mp4
    <name>_<traj>_scale<scale_factor>_<MMDDHHMM>_depth.mp4
```

注意 out_name = f'{name}_{traj}_scale{scale_factor}_{time.strftime("%m%d%H%M")}'，name 是 config 文件名（去掉路径和 .yaml）。

video 文件命名：`{video_prefix}_{k}.mp4`，k in ['depth', 'normal', 'color', 'flow']。所以实际生成 `<name>_arc_scale1.0_08311234_color.mp4` 和 `_depth.mp4`（normal 和 flow 缺文件会跳过打印 "Images missing for tag"）。

关键细节：
- `create_videos(base_dir=traj_dir, input_dir=traj_dir, out_name=..., num_frames=n_frames)`：base_dir 和 input_dir 都是 traj_dir。
- `zpad = max(5, len(str(num_frames - 1)))`：480-1=479，len=3，zpad=5。与 export_image 中的 `'{0:05d}'.format(idx)` 一致。
- depth 视频：`render_dist_curve_fn = np.log`，lo/hi 从**第 0 帧彩色图**的 3%/97% 分位取 log 得到（注意是从 color frame 算的，这看起来有点怪，实际上是代码从 mipnerf360 继承的做法——原版是对 depth 取分位，这里改成了对 color frame 取，这可能是一个 bug 或者故意的行为。让我仔细看：

```python
color_file = os.path.join(input_dir, 'renders', f'{idx_to_str(0)}.png')
color_frame = load_img(color_file)
shape = color_frame.shape
p = 3
distance_limits = np.percentile(color_frame.flatten(), [p, 100 - p])
lo, hi = [render_dist_curve_fn(x) for x in distance_limits]
```

确实是从 color frame 算的。这继承自 Google mipnerf360 的 create_videos，原版：
```python
# Load one example frame to get image shape and depth range.
depth_file = os.path.join(input_dir, f'{name}_1.tiff')
depth_frame = load_img(depth_file)[..., 0]
shape = depth_frame.shape
distance_limits = np.percentile(depth_frame, [p, 100 - p])
```
原版是从 depth frame 算分位。这里被改成了 color_frame。所以 lo/hi 实际上来自渲染第一帧的亮度分位（log 后），然后用这个范围归一化 log(depth)。这是一个可以指出的细节——lo/hi 的来源从原版的深度图变成了彩色图，因此深度视频的对比度拉伸基准其实是第一帧颜色的 log 分位。这对教学有价值，但我需要小心陈述：就说「lo/hi 由第 0 帧渲染彩色图的 3%/97% 分位取对数得到，再用它归一化 log 深度」，可以指出这与深度本身无关，是继承代码改造的痕迹。我不应过度断言它是 bug，但可以指出「值得注意」。

- depth colormap：`cm.get_cmap('turbo')(img)[..., :3]`
- 帧写入：`(np.clip(np.nan_to_num(img), 0., 1.) * 255.).astype(np.uint8)`
- mediapy `media.VideoWriter(video_file, shape=shape[:2], codec='h264', fps=48, crf=18, input_format='rgb')`。注意 shape[:2] 是 (H, W)。mediapy 要求 shape 为 (height, width)。
- input_format = 'gray' if k == 'alpha' else 'rgb'——但循环里 k 只有 depth/normal/color/flow，没有 alpha，所以恒为 rgb。

- `reconstruction(cam_traj, traj_dir, stage="trajectory")`：stage != "validation" 时走 `render_pkg = self.render(viewpoint_cam.cuda(), self.gaussians)`，即直接用 Camera 对象（不是 (gt, cam) 元组）。注意 cam_traj 里的 Camera 是 deepcopy 的模板相机，其 image 字段——deepcopy 了 viewpoint_cameras[0][1]，这个相机来自 getAllCameras()。注意 getAllCameras 返回的相机是否带图？让我检查 scene/__init__.py 的 getAllCameras。

我需要确认 getAllCameras 返回什么格式（是 (gt, cam) 元组还是 Camera 对象）。从 generate_path 中 `cam[1].world_view_transform` 看，输入是 (gt_image, cam) 元组格式？不对，等等：

```python
c2ws = np.array([np.linalg.inv(np.asarray((cam[1].world_view_transform.T).cpu().numpy())) 
                 for cam in viewpoint_cameras])
```

是 `cam[1].world_view_transform`，所以 getAllCameras() 返回的是 (gt, cam) 元组列表？这很奇怪。让我查一下 scene/__init__.py。

而 reconstruction 中 stage != "validation" 时：
```python
render_pkg = self.render(viewpoint_cam.cuda(), self.gaussians)
```
viewpoint_cam 是 cam_traj 的元素，cam_traj 是 Camera 对象列表（generate_path 返回 `traj` 列表，元素是 deepcopy 的 Camera）。所以轨迹模式下直接传 Camera。

但 `viewpoint_cam.cuda()` 对 Camera 对象——Camera 类有 cuda 方法吗？让我检查 scene/cameras.py。u7-l2 摘要说「再克隆锚点相机产出 480 个新 Camera（内参继承、宽高取偶）」。

而 validation 模式时 `viewpoint_cam[1].cuda()`——说明 getTestCameras() 返回 (gt, cam) 元组。这与 4DGS 的习惯一致：4DGS 的 dataset 里 getTestCameras 返回 [(gt_image, cam), ...]。

我需要验证：
1. scene/__init__.py 中 getAllCameras / getTestCameras 返回什么
2. scene/cameras.py 中 Camera.cuda() 是否存在，deepcopy 时 gt_image 是否被复制（显存问题）

另外还需要检查 render.py 中 traj 分支的具体行号，以及 gaussian_renderer/__init__.py 的 render 签名（viewpoint_cam, pipe, bg_color, ...）来解释 partial(render, pipe=pipe, bg_color=background)。

还要确认 render() 返回 dict 中的 'depth' 键。

让我读这些文件。

另外注意 mesh_utils.py 中 reconstruction 在 stage=="trajectory" 时也会做 export 吗？不会，render.py 分两步调用：reconstruction(...)（把 rgbmaps/depthmaps 存内存）然后 export_image(traj_dir, mode="trajectory")。mode 参数其实没被用（export_image 的 mode 参数未使用）。

好，现在让我读 scene/__init__.py 和 scene/cameras.py 的相关部分来确认接口。

import torch
from torch.nn import functional as F
import math
from diff_gaussian_rasterization import GaussianRasterizationSettings, GaussianRasterizer
from scene.gaussian_model import GaussianModel
from utils.sh_utils import eval_sh, eval_shfs_4d

def render(viewpoint_camera, pc: GaussianModel, pipe, bg_color: torch.Tensor, scaling_modifier=1.0, override_color=None, args=None, iteration=-1):
    """
    Render the scene. 
    Background tensor (bg_color) must be on GPU!
    """
 
    # Create zero tensor. We will use it to make pytorch return gradients of the 2D (screen-space) means
    screenspace_points = torch.zeros_like(pc.get_xyz, dtype=pc.get_xyz.dtype, requires_grad=True, device="cuda") + 0
    try:
        screenspace_points.retain_grad()
    except:
        pass

    # Set up rasterization configuration
    tanfovx = math.tan(viewpoint_camera.FoVx * 0.5)
    tanfovy = math.tan(viewpoint_camera.FoVy * 0.5)

    raster_settings = GaussianRasterizationSettings(
        image_height=int(viewpoint_camera.image_height),
        image_width=int(viewpoint_camera.image_width),
        tanfovx=tanfovx,
        tanfovy=tanfovy,
        bg=bg_color if not pipe.env_map_res else torch.zeros(3, device="cuda"),
        scale_modifier=scaling_modifier,
        viewmatrix=viewpoint_camera.world_view_transform,
        projmatrix=viewpoint_camera.full_proj_transform,
        sh_degree=pc.active_sh_degree,
        sh_degree_t=pc.active_sh_degree_t,
        campos=viewpoint_camera.camera_center,
        timestamp=viewpoint_camera.timestamp,
        time_duration=pc.time_duration[1]-pc.time_duration[0],
        rot_4d=pc.rot_4d,
        gaussian_dim=pc.gaussian_dim,
        force_sh_3d=pc.force_sh_3d,
        prefiltered=False,
        debug=pipe.debug,
    )

    rasterizer = GaussianRasterizer(raster_settings=raster_settings)

    means3D = pc.get_xyz
    means2D = screenspace_points
    opacity = pc.get_opacity
    
    # opacity decay
    if (args is not None) and args.opacity_decay and (iteration > args.decay_from_iter):
        if args.time_aware:
            space_visibility = rasterizer.markVisible(means3D)
            time_visibility = pc.get_marginal_t(viewpoint_camera.timestamp)[:,0] > 0.05 
            visibility = space_visibility & time_visibility
            visibility = visibility.view(-1, 1)
        else:
            visibility = None
        
        # Apply opacity decay to Gaussians that are visible in current view
        visible_opacities = pc.opacity_decay(f_min=args.f_min, f_max=args.f_max, mask=visibility)        
        opacity = visible_opacities

    # If precomputed 3d covariance is provided, use it. If not, then it will be computed from
    # scaling / rotation by the rasterizer.
    scales = None
    scales_t = None
    rotations = None
    rotations_r = None
    ts = None
    cov3D_precomp = None
    if pipe.compute_cov3D_python:
        if pc.rot_4d:
            cov3D_precomp, delta_mean = pc.get_current_covariance_and_mean_offset(scaling_modifier, viewpoint_camera.timestamp)
            means3D = means3D + delta_mean
        else:
            cov3D_precomp = pc.get_covariance(scaling_modifier)
        if pc.gaussian_dim == 4:
            marginal_t = pc.get_marginal_t(viewpoint_camera.timestamp)
            opacity = opacity * marginal_t
    else:
        scales = pc.get_scaling
        rotations = pc.get_rotation
        if pc.gaussian_dim == 4:
            scales_t = pc.get_scaling_t
            ts = pc.get_t
            if pc.rot_4d:
                rotations_r = pc.get_rotation_r

    # If precomputed colors are provided, use them. Otherwise, if it is desired to precompute colors
    # from SHs in Python, do it. If not, then SH -> RGB conversion will be done by rasterizer.
    shs = None
    colors_precomp = None
    if override_color is None:
        if pipe.convert_SHs_python:
            shs_view = pc.get_features.transpose(1, 2).view(-1, 3, pc.get_max_sh_channels)
            if pipe.compute_cov3D_python:
                dir_pp = (means3D - viewpoint_camera.camera_center.repeat(pc.get_features.shape[0], 1)).detach()
            else:
                _, delta_mean = pc.get_current_covariance_and_mean_offset(scaling_modifier, viewpoint_camera.timestamp)
                dir_pp = ((means3D + delta_mean) - viewpoint_camera.camera_center.repeat(pc.get_features.shape[0], 1)).detach()
            dir_pp_normalized = dir_pp/dir_pp.norm(dim=1, keepdim=True)
            if pc.gaussian_dim == 3 or pc.force_sh_3d:
                sh2rgb = eval_sh(pc.active_sh_degree, shs_view, dir_pp_normalized)
            elif pc.gaussian_dim == 4:
                dir_t = (pc.get_t - viewpoint_camera.timestamp).detach()
                sh2rgb = eval_shfs_4d(pc.active_sh_degree, pc.active_sh_degree_t, shs_view, dir_pp_normalized, dir_t, pc.time_duration[1] - pc.time_duration[0])
            colors_precomp = torch.clamp_min(sh2rgb + 0.5, 0.0)
        else:
            shs = pc.get_features
            if pc.gaussian_dim == 4 and ts is None:
                ts = pc.get_t
    else:
        colors_precomp = override_color
    
    flow_2d = torch.zeros_like(pc.get_xyz[:,:2])
    
    # Prefilter
    if pipe.compute_cov3D_python and pc.gaussian_dim == 4:
        mask = marginal_t[:,0] > 0.05
        if means2D is not None:
            means2D = means2D[mask]
        if means3D is not None:
            means3D = means3D[mask]
        if ts is not None:
            ts = ts[mask]
        if shs is not None:
            shs = shs[mask]
        if colors_precomp is not None:
            colors_precomp = colors_precomp[mask]
        if opacity is not None:
            opacity = opacity[mask]
        if scales is not None:
            scales = scales[mask]
        if scales_t is not None:
            scales_t = scales_t[mask]
        if rotations is not None:
            rotations = rotations[mask]
        if rotations_r is not None:
            rotations_r = rotations_r[mask]
        if cov3D_precomp is not None:
            cov3D_precomp = cov3D_precomp[mask]
        if flow_2d is not None:
            flow_2d = flow_2d[mask]
    
    # Rasterize visible Gaussians to image, obtain their radii (on screen). 
    rendered_image, radii, depth, alpha, flow, covs_com = rasterizer(
        means3D = means3D,
        means2D = means2D,
        shs = shs,
        colors_precomp = colors_precomp,
        flow_2d = flow_2d,
        opacities = opacity,
        ts = ts,
        scales = scales,
        scales_t = scales_t,
        rotations = rotations,
        rotations_r = rotations_r,
        cov3D_precomp = cov3D_precomp)
    
    if pipe.env_map_res:
        assert pc.env_map is not None
        R = 60
        rays_o, rays_d = viewpoint_camera.get_rays()
        delta = ((rays_o*rays_d).sum(-1))**2 - (rays_d**2).sum(-1)*((rays_o**2).sum(-1)-R**2)
        assert (delta > 0).all()
        t_inter = -(rays_o*rays_d).sum(-1)+torch.sqrt(delta)/(rays_d**2).sum(-1)
        xyz_inter = rays_o + rays_d * t_inter.unsqueeze(-1)
        tu = torch.atan2(xyz_inter[...,1:2], xyz_inter[...,0:1]) / (2 * torch.pi) + 0.5 # theta
        tv = torch.acos(xyz_inter[...,2:3] / R) / torch.pi
        texcoord = torch.cat([tu, tv], dim=-1) * 2 - 1
        bg_color_from_envmap = F.grid_sample(pc.env_map[None], texcoord[None])[0] # 3,H,W
        # mask2 = (0 < xyz_inter[...,0]) & (xyz_inter[...,1] > 0) # & (xyz_inter[...,2] > -19)
        rendered_image = rendered_image + (1 - alpha) * bg_color_from_envmap # * mask2[None]
    
    if pipe.compute_cov3D_python and pc.gaussian_dim == 4:
        radii_all = radii.new_zeros(mask.shape)
        radii_all[mask] = radii
    else:
        radii_all = radii
        
    visibility_filter = radii_all > 0

    # Those Gaussians that were frustum culled or had a radius of 0 were not visible.
    # They will be excluded from value updates used in the splitting criteria.
    return {"render": rendered_image,
            "viewspace_points": screenspace_points,
            "visibility_filter" : visibility_filter,
            "radii": radii_all,
            "depth": depth,
            "alpha": alpha,
            "flow": flow}

from matplotlib import scale
import torch
from torch import nn
import numpy as np
from utils.graphics_utils import getWorld2View2, getProjectionMatrix, getProjectionMatrixCenterShift
from kornia import create_meshgrid
from copy import deepcopy

class Camera:
    def __init__(self, colmap_id, R, T, FoVx, FoVy, image, gt_alpha_mask,
                 image_name, uid,
                 trans=np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.0]), scale=1.0, data_device = "cuda", timestamp = 0.0,
                 cx=-1, cy=-1, fl_x=-1, fl_y=-1, depth=None, resolution=None, image_path=None, meta_only=False,
                 ):

        self.uid = uid
        self.colmap_id = colmap_id
        self.R = R
        self.T = T
        self.FoVx = FoVx
        self.FoVy = FoVy
        self.image_name = image_name
        self.cx = cx
        self.cy = cy
        self.fl_x = fl_x
        self.fl_y = fl_y
        self.resolution = resolution
        self.image_path = image_path
        self.image = image
        self.gt_alpha_mask = gt_alpha_mask
        self.meta_only = meta_only
        
        try:
            self.data_device = torch.device(data_device)
        except Exception as e:
            print(e)
            print(f"[Warning] Custom device {data_device} failed, fallback to default cuda device")
            self.data_device = torch.device("cuda")

        self.image_width = resolution[0]
        self.image_height = resolution[1]
        
        if not self.meta_only:
            if gt_alpha_mask is not None:
                self.image *= gt_alpha_mask.to(self.image.device)
            else:
                self.image *= torch.ones((1, self.image_height, self.image_width), device=self.image.device)

        self.zfar = 100.0
        self.znear = 0.01

        self.trans = trans
        self.scale = scale

        self.world_view_transform = torch.tensor(getWorld2View2(R, T, trans, scale)).transpose(0, 1)
        if cx > 0:
            self.projection_matrix = getProjectionMatrixCenterShift(self.znear, self.zfar, cx, cy, fl_x, fl_y, self.image_width, self.image_height).transpose(0,1)
        else:
            self.projection_matrix = getProjectionMatrix(znear=self.znear, zfar=self.zfar, fovX=self.FoVx, fovY=self.FoVy).transpose(0,1)
        self.full_proj_transform = (self.world_view_transform.unsqueeze(0).bmm(self.projection_matrix.unsqueeze(0))).squeeze(0)
        self.camera_center = self.world_view_transform.inverse()[3, :3]
        
        self.timestamp = timestamp
        
    def get_rays(self):
        grid = create_meshgrid(self.image_height, self.image_width, normalized_coordinates=False)[0] + 0.5
        i, j = grid.unbind(-1)
        pts_view = torch.stack([(i-self.cx)/self.fl_x, (j-self.cy)/self.fl_y, torch.ones_like(i), torch.ones_like(i)], -1).to(self.data_device)
        c2w = torch.linalg.inv(self.world_view_transform.transpose(0, 1))
        pts_world =  pts_view @ c2w.T
        directions = pts_world[...,:3] - self.camera_center[None,None,:]
        return self.camera_center[None,None], directions / torch.norm(directions, dim=-1, keepdim=True)
    
    def cuda(self):
        cuda_copy = deepcopy(self)
        for k, v in cuda_copy.__dict__.items():
            if isinstance(v, torch.Tensor):
                cuda_copy.__dict__[k] = v.to(cuda_copy.data_device)
        return cuda_copy
    
    
class MiniCam:
    def __init__(self, width, height, fovy, fovx, znear, zfar, world_view_transform, full_proj_transform):
        self.image_width = width
        self.image_height = height    
        self.FoVy = fovy
        self.FoVx = fovx
        self.znear = znear
        self.zfar = zfar
        self.world_view_transform = world_view_transform
        self.full_proj_transform = full_proj_transform
        view_inv = torch.inverse(self.world_view_transform)
        self.camera_center = view_inv[3][:3]

返回 CameraDataset（train + test 相机列表拷贝）。generate_path 里用 `cam[1]` 索引，说明它假设传入的是可索引的 (image, cam) 元组序列——CameraDataset 支持 `viewpoint_cameras[i]`（Python 的 Dataset 重载了 `__getitem__`），返回 `(viewpoint_image, viewpoint_cam)`。所以 `[viewpoint_cameras[i] for i in range(0, len(...), total_frames)]` 这个列表推导会对 CameraDataset 逐个调用 `__getitem__`，触发懒加载（meta_only 时 cv2.imread）！也就是说 generate_path 采样锚点时会把锚点帧的图像读进来（虽然后面只用位姿）。这个值得注意——range(0, len, total_frames) 在 total_frames=300 时会取 idx 0, 300, 600, ...（len 是 4×300=1200 时取 4 个）。

渲染 480 帧 arc 轨迹视频，用 ffmpeg 每 40 帧抽帧拼网格图，检查运动区域跨帧一致性，并解释为什么轨迹渲染必须绕过训练循环直接调用 render()。

我需要给出具体命令：
```bash
python render.py --config configs/dynerf/flame_steak.yaml --traj arc \
    --start_checkpoint <训练目录>/chkpnt30000.pth \
    --training_view 1,10,13,20 --total_frames 300
```
注意 render.py 的参数：--traj、--scale、--start_checkpoint、--training_view、--total_frames。还要注意 render.py 默认 gaussian_dim=3，必须带 --config 让 yaml 覆盖（u7-l1 摘要已建立这个认知）。

抽帧网格：
```bash

```
480 帧 / 40 = 12 帧 → 4×3 网格。

关于「为什么轨迹渲染必须绕过训练循环直接调用 render()」，我要从源码给出论证：
1. 训练循环（train.py training()）的数据源是 DataLoader（scene.getTrainCameras()），每个 batch 元素是 (gt_image, cam) 元组，且 loss 需要 GT 图像；轨迹相机是 generate_path 合成的，世界上不存在对应照片，没有 GT，无法进入 loss 计算。
2. 训练循环会更新参数（optimizer.step、致密化、opacity decay 写回 _opacity.data）；轨迹渲染的目的恰恰是「冻结现场」评估当前场，任何参数更新都会污染评估。@torch.no_grad() 装饰（reconstruction L107、export_image L216）+ partial 固定 args=None/iteration=-1 使 render 内的 opacity decay 分支（gaussian_renderer/__init__.py L64 条件 args is not None）恒不触发。
3. 训练循环按 iteration 终止、按 batch 组织；轨迹渲染按帧列表组织（480 个相机一次性传入）。
4. depth 导出：训练循环不消费 render_pkg['depth']，而 GaussianExtractor 消费。

关于 mediapy：create_videos 用 mediapy（import mediapy as media，L19）。VideoWriter 参数 shape=(H,W)、codec h264、fps 48、crf 18、input_format rgb。fps=48 与 n_frames=480 → 视频时长 10 秒，恰与 time_duration [0,10] 同长——这是一个很优雅的对应：timestamp = 10*i/480，即每帧 1/48 秒 × 480 帧 = 10 s 覆盖时间域 [0,10)。哇，这个对应值得写：48 fps × 480 帧 = 10 秒 = time_duration 长度，所以视频播放速度等于场景时间流速（1:1 实时回放）。这解释了 fps=48 不是随便选的。

等等，让我验证：轨迹 timestamp = 10.0/n_frames * i = 10i/480。第 i 帧对应场景时刻 10i/480。视频第 i 帧的播放时刻是 i/48 秒。若要回放速度等于场景时间流速（秒对秒），需要 10i/480 场景单位 = i/48 秒 → 10/480 = 1/48 ✓。完美。所以 fps=48 让视频以 1:1 的「场景时间 : 现实时间」回放。不过 time_duration 是抽象时间单位（入口默认 [-0.5,0.5]，官方 yaml 是 [0,10]），对 dynerf 数据 300 帧，10 单位 ÷ 300 帧 = 1/30 单位/帧，即数据帧率 30fps。所以场景的 1 时间单位 = 3 现实秒（30fps 数据）。hmm，这样的话 fps=48 的视频是「加速」回放？

再想：数据 300 帧在 time 域 [0,10) 均匀分布 → 数据相邻帧间隔 Δt=10/300=1/30。如果数据是 30fps 视频，则 1/30 时间单位 = 1/30 秒 → 1 单位 = 1 秒。那么轨迹 480 帧覆盖 10 单位 = 10 秒场景时间；视频 480 帧 @48fps = 10 秒。所以 1:1 实时。前提是源视频 30fps。N3V/DyNeRF 数据确实是 30fps。所以 fps=48 × 480 帧 = 10 秒视频对应 10 秒场景时间 = 实时回放。这个推理链合理，但我应该谨慎表述：说明 fps=48 与 480 帧的乘积恰为 10 秒、与 time_duration 长度 10 一致，回放速率与数据 30fps 的采集速率一致（可标注为推导，不必断言作者意图）。

我会表述为：480 帧 / 48 fps = 10 s，与 time_duration 长度 10 一致；数据侧 300 帧铺满同一 [0,10) 域相当于 30 fps，因此视频回放的时间流速与采集速率一致（每单位时间 30 帧 vs 视频 48 帧铺 10 单位——不对！）。

等一下，我要重新算。数据：300 帧映射到 [0,10)，每帧 Δt = 10/300 ≈ 0.0333 单位。若源视频 30 fps，则每帧 1/30 s ≈ 0.0333 s。所以 1 单位 ≈ 1 s（若源是 30fps）。

视频：480 帧映射到 [0,10)（timestamp=10i/480），每帧 Δt = 10/480 ≈ 0.02083 单位 ≈ 0.02083 s（按 1单位=1s）。视频帧间隔 1/48 s ≈ 0.02083 s。✓ 完全一致。所以视频是实时回放（时间流速 1:1）。好，fps=48 与 n_frames=480、time_duration=10 三者构成自洽的实时回放。这个分析我可以写进 create_videos 模块，作为「为什么是 48」的解释，标注这是从参数数值推出的关系。

# GaussianExtractor and Video Export

## 1. Learning Objectives of This Lecture
## 2. Prerequisites
- Recap of the trajectory camera output from u7-l2
- functools.partial
- @torch.no_grad()
- PNG uint8 vs TIFF float32
- mediapy / h264 / crf / fps
- colormap (turbo)
## 3. Source Code Map of This Lecture
## 4. Core Concepts and Source Code Explanation

### 4.1 The traj Branch in render.py: a Four-Step Pipeline
4.1.1 Concept
4.1.2 Pipeline
4.1.3 Source Code Close Reading (render.py L63-75, L57-61, L163)
4.1.4 Practice (run the trajectory rendering command, observe directory structure)
4.1.5 Exercises

### 4.2 GaussianExtractor: Batch Rendering with a partial-Wrapped render()
4.2.1 Concept
4.2.2 Pipeline
4.2.3 Source Code Close Reading (__init__ L82-95, clean, reconstruction L107-154; comparison with reconstruction_and_export; no_grad; args=None so decay does not trigger)
4.2.4 Practice (add frame-count printing; CPU memory accounting)
4.2.5 Exercises

### 4.3 export_image: Two Kinds of Files Landing on Disk
4.3.1 Concept (renders png + vis tiff)
4.3.2 Pipeline
4.3.3 Source Code Close Reading (L216-225, save_img_u8/f32 L512-521)
4.3.4 Practice (use PIL to read back a tiff and inspect float32 depth values)
4.2.5 Exercises

### 4.4 create_videos: From Frames to mp4
4.4.1 Concept
4.4.2 Pipeline
4.4.3 Source Code Close Reading (L443-510)
4.4.4 Practice (the ffmpeg frame-extraction grid)
4.4.5 Exercises

## 5. Comprehensive Practice (grid of one frame every 40 frames + cross-frame consistency + explanation of why it bypasses the training loop)
## 6. Summary of This Lecture
## 7. Next-Step Learning Suggestions

Note that exercise 4.1.4 should not duplicate the comprehensive practice. 4.1.4 can be "dry-run observation of directory structure + interpret out_name"; the comprehensive practice is the complete ffmpeg grid + consistency analysis.

Explain "why trajectory rendering must bypass the training loop and call render() directly" — placed in 4.2 (GaussianExtractor's design intent), and then summarized again in the comprehensive practice.

Writing style control: concise, don't pile on large blocks of source code.

Content points:
1. Pipeline: generate_path (480 Cameras) → reconstruction (rendering into memory) → export_image (renders/*.png + vis/depth_*.tiff) → create_videos (color/depth mp4)
2. GaussianExtractor design:
   - partial(render, pipe=pipe, bg_color=background) fixes the render signature's pipe and bg_color; when called self.render(cam.cuda(), self.gaussians)
   - bg_color is determined by white_background (render.py L42), note the default [0,0,0]
   - @torch.no_grad(): no gradient graph built
   - render's args defaults to None → the opacity decay branch (gaussian_renderer L64) never triggers → the trajectory rendering only reads the decay already accumulated in _opacity
   - The dual mode of reconstruction: in validation stage, element = (gt, cam) tuple; in trajectory stage, element = Camera
   - A side detail: the LPIPS network is constructed unconditionally (L116-118), even for trajectories; weights are downloaded on the first run
   - The reason for existence of reconstruction_and_export: rendering and writing simultaneously to save memory (the 480-frame rgbmaps+depthmaps memory accounting)
3. The reason for bypassing the training loop:
   - The training loop requires (gt_image, cam) to compute loss; the trajectory camera is synthesized with no GT
   - The training loop updates parameters (optimizer.step / densification / opacity decay write-back); the trajectory exists for frozen evaluation
   - The training loop terminates by iteration; the trajectory is a pure frame list
4. export_image:
   - rgbmaps[idx].permute(1,2,0): CHW→HWC, [0,1] float → uint8 PNG
   - depthmaps[idx][0]: take the first channel → float32 TIFF
   - mode parameter is actually unused
   - 5-digit numbering consistent with create_videos' zpad=5
5. create_videos:
   - mediapy VideoWriter: shape=(H,W), codec h264, fps 48, crf 18, input_format rgb
   - The elegant correspondence between fps=48 and 480 frames: the video duration is 480/48=10s, equal to the time_duration length of 10; data with 300 frames spread over [0,10) corresponds to 30fps, so the video playback time flow matches the capture rate
   - color: renders/{idx:05d}.png /255
   - depth: vis/depth_{idx:05d}.tiff → log → normalize with lo/hi → turbo
   - lo/hi actually comes from the percentile range of color frame 0 (the comment says depth range, the code reads color_file) — point out this detail
   - normal/flow are always skipped (render does not produce such files)
   - L498 ValueError is constructed but not raised
   - Why width/height are rounded to even: yuv420/h264 requires even dimensions
6. Output structure tree:
```
output/N3V/flame_steak/traj/ours_30000/
├── renders/00000.png ... 00479.png
├── vis/depth_00000.tiff ... depth_00479.tiff
├── flame_steak_arc_scale1.0_<MMDDHHMM>_color.mp4
└── flame_steak_arc_scale1.0_<MMDDHHMM>_depth.mp4
```
7. Points for locating time-inconsistent regions: color video freezes/jumps/flickers in moving regions; the depth video is more sensitive (depth discontinuity jitter)

Command-line example:
```bash
python render.py --config configs/dynerf/flame_steak.yaml \
    --start_checkpoint output/N3V/flame_steak/chkpnt30000.pth \
    --training_view 1,10,13,20 --total_frames 300 --traj arc
```
Note: render.py's --traj default None; both traj/validate cannot be empty (L193 assert). --scale defaults to 1.0. resolution comes from the yaml's 2.

ffmpeg frame extraction:
```bash
ffmpeg -i traj/ours_30000/flame_steak_arc_scale1.0_*_color.mp4 \
  -vf "select='not(mod(n\,40))',scale=320:-2,tile=4x3" -frames:v 1 grid.png
```
Note that in ffmpeg filter syntax, commas inside select must be escaped. Or use fps=48/40=1.2. Simpler:
`-vf "select=not(mod(n\,40)),scale=iw/4:-1,tile=4x3"` needs -vsync vfr. Let me give a command that can actually run:

```bash
ffmpeg -i input.mp4 -vf "select='not(mod(n,40))',scale=320:-2,tile=4x3" -frames:v 1 grid.png
```
Inside -vf, the commas in mod(n,40) conflict with filter separator commas, so they must be escaped as mod(n\,40) or wrapped in quotes. select='not(mod(n,40))' — when the whole filter string is already inside shell double quotes, ffmpeg internally parses filter separators by commas, and the commas inside mod() are ambiguous. The common safe approach is:
`-vf "select='not(mod(n\,40))',scale=320:-2,tile=4x3"`
In the shell, the \, inside double quotes is passed as \, to ffmpeg, and ffmpeg's filter parser interprets \, as a literal comma. This is common practice. Alternatively, use Python + PIL to extract frames, avoiding escaping issues. To be safe, I'll give both approaches: ffmpeg (with escaping noted) and a pure Python fallback (decord/imageio may not be installed; using imageio may not be installed either; using PIL to splice a grid from pngs in renders/ is actually the easiest! Since renders/ already has 480 pngs, every 40th frame directly reads 00000.png, 00040.png, ... with PIL and splices the grid, completely bypassing ffmpeg).

Good idea: the comprehensive practice offers two options: A) ffmpeg extracts from the mp4; B) directly use PIL to read every 40th png from renders/ and splice the grid (no ffmpeg dependency). Option B is actually more stable and tests understanding of the output structure. I'll give example code for Option B (marked as "example code").

12 frames × spacing 40: 0,40,...,440 → exactly 12 frames, 4×3 grid.

Cross-frame consistency check points:
- Whether the flame/steak edges stay sharp in adjacent frames of the moving region or show trailing/ghosting (temporal trailing caused by 4D Gaussian time scales being too large)
- Whether abrupt changes appear in unobserved regions between training views (the arc stays within the observed arc segment, fewer such issues; ellipse would show them)
- Depth video: whether the moving region's depth flickers

Answers to the exercises:
4.1.5:
1) Why out_name embeds time.strftime("%m%d%H%M")? → Avoid overwriting videos from different runs of the same trajectory and same scale; the output name of each run carries the timestamp of the run (accurate to the minute), making it easy to compare multiple experiment videos side by side.
2) n_frames is hardcoded to 480, what do I change to get 320 frames? → render.py L66; but need to be careful: timestamp=10.0/n_frames*i will re-map the time domain, so with fps=48 unchanged the video duration becomes 320/48≈6.67s, and the playback rate no longer matches the capture rate.
3) What happens if --traj and --validate are both omitted? → L193 assert fails, reporting "No validation or trajectory rendering requested".

4.2.5:
1) Why does partial fix pipe and bg_color rather than passing them per call? → render's signature is (viewpoint_camera, pc, pipe, bg_color, ...); within one evaluation task these two are constant for all frames; fixing them once yields a unified two-argument interface self.render(cam, gaussians); it also prevents accidental inconsistency of pipe/bg across frames.
2) In trajectory mode why does args=None cause opacity decay not to trigger? Cite gaussian_renderer L64's condition (args is not None) and args.opacity_decay and iteration > decay_from_iter. Iteration defaults to -1, so even if args is passed, -1 > 500 does not hold.
3) About the LPIPS network being constructed unconditionally.

4.3.5:
1) Why is depth stored as TIFF float32 instead of PNG? → Depth is continuous physical quantities (not limited to [0,1]), uint8 quantization would lose precision; save_img_f32 preserves raw float32.
2) depthmaps[idx][0] taking channel 0 means what about the shape (depth is a single-channel (1,H,W)).
3) What happens if reconstruction is called twice without clean in between? → clean() is called at the start of reconstruction, self-cleaning.

4.4.5:
1) Why is the depth video colored with turbo? → Log depth is single channel; pseudo-color mapping enhances human discrimination of depth differences.
2) The four kinds k only actually produce two — normal/flow are skipped because vis/ has no normal_*.tiff and no flow directory.
3) What happens if frames are missing? → L497-498 only constructs a ValueError without raising it, actually load_img crashes with FileNotFoundError when opening the file (or is it that the earlier os.path.exists check for file0 only checks frame 0?). Note: create_videos only checks the file0 existence of each category (L483-485); intermediate missing frames have no check; L497's if not os.path.exists(img_file): ValueError(...) constructs without raising, so they fall through to load_img → FileNotFoundError in open(). The behavior is a crash. This is the answer.

OK, content is ready. One more thing: in the traj branch of validation(), generate_path's first argument is scene.getAllCameras() (train+test concatenated). getAllCameras returns a CameraDataset (not a plain list). Indexing in generate_path triggers __getitem__ (lazy loading of images). When the trajectory renders 480 frames of Camera, it deepcopies viewpoint_cameras[0][1] — note the elements retrieved from CameraDataset are (image, cam) tuples, so [1] is Camera.

The cost of deepcopy: meta_only=True (dataloader=True when binding, camera_utils.py L68) → image=None → lightweight. But note that in generate_path's L386 list comprehension, __getitem__ has already loaded the anchor frame image into memory (data_utils L12-19), then only cam[1] is used and the image is discarded. A small waste, but worth pointing out.

Regarding the estimate_bounding_sphere / extract_mesh_bounded / post_process_mesh / to_cam_open3d and other mesh-related functions in mesh_utils.py: the file is called mesh_utils, and GaussianExtractor's docstring also mentions export_mesh_bounded, but the 4C4D trajectory workflow only uses reconstruction/export_image/reconstruction_and_export. I should mention in the source map that "the mesh extraction part (TSDF fusion) is inherited from the 2DGS project, and this lecture only covers the image/video pipeline" — to avoid reader confusion. In the class docstring (L84-89) it says "a class that extracts attributes a scene presented by 2DGS", which shows it was migrated from 2DGS.
